_note: W14 moral-circle sequence, decided by Roger 2026-10-09.  Apply in the batch: descriptions below (selfish by the rewritten-pair procedure, the rest keep their non-X labels and their sequence arrangement), then the sequence rewritten to the order below, and philanthropic, patriotic, cosmopolitan set to singletons.  Then the label-blind naming check on every rewritten member (Roger's naming rule), ethnocentric and insular first.

descriptions.selfish: This means prioritizing one's own interests, desires, and wellbeing above those of others, showing little concern for how one's actions affect other people.
descriptions.clannish: This means putting one's own family first: caring about one's kin, close and distant, above everyone else, and treating anyone outside the family as not one's concern.
descriptions.cliqueish: This means putting one's own circle of friends and family first: caring about the few people one spends one's time with above everyone else, and being exclusionary, dismissive, or uncaring toward outsiders.
descriptions.parochial: This means putting one's own town or parish first: caring about the people who live there above everyone else, and treating anyone from a few towns over as not one's concern.
descriptions.insular: This means putting one's own city or home state first: caring about the people there above those of the rest of the country, and treating anyone from another city or state as not one's concern.
descriptions.regionalist: This means putting one's own region of the country first: caring about its people, its interests, and its ways above those of the rest of the country, favoring locals over outsiders, and treating people from other regions as not one's concern.
descriptions.sectarian: This means putting one's own faith first: caring about fellow believers above everyone else, and treating people of other faiths or denominations as not one's concern.
descriptions.nationalist: This means putting one's own nation first: caring about its people and its interests above those of any other country, and treating foreigners as not one's concern.
descriptions.ethnocentric: This means drawing one's moral circle at one's own racial group: weighing the welfare of those who share one's race above everyone else's, and treating people of other races as not one's concern.
